questions.prompt: Three calls at second 59 and three at 61 pass a three-per-calendar-minute limit. What does this demonstrate?

options.label: A calendar-window limit can allow both batches; it does not enforce the stated rolling-window contract.
It proves at most three calls in every rolling 60 seconds.
The algorithm is defective even if the product explicitly allows calendar-boundary bursts.

questions.explanation: Match the selected algorithm to the promised interval. A calendar quota may be correct for its contract while violating a strict rolling promise.

questions.prompt: For the authored rolling interval, how are equal-time calls and the exact 60-second boundary counted?

options.label: Retain distinct accepted attempts inside (now - 60, now]; an attempt exactly 60 seconds old has expired.
Collapse equal timestamps into one attempt to save memory.
Keep every attempt at or before now forever.

questions.explanation: The open lower boundary expires an attempt exactly one period old. Each admitted attempt has its own log entry even when timestamps match.

questions.prompt: A bucket has capacity 3 and refills 3 tokens per 90 seconds. Does it guarantee no more than 3 admissions in every rolling 90 seconds?

options.label: A full bucket can admit a burst; its capacity and refill rate do not promise a strict rolling-window count.
Its refill rate proves the same limit for every rolling window.
Idle time must accumulate unlimited burst capacity.

questions.explanation: The fixture admits 3 immediately and another after 30 seconds; capacity caps idle credit, but the contract differs from a strict rolling log.

questions.prompt: An API admits ten requests per second, but each holds a scarce downstream slot for a long time. What else must be defined?

options.label: Use an in-flight limit with bounded admission and release; a request rate alone does not bound simultaneous slow work.
A per-second counter proves at most ten operations are in flight.
Rate tokens authorize any operation requested by that client.

questions.explanation: Rate, in-flight capacity, authorization and idempotency are distinct contracts. Define slot ownership, deadlines and release under failure/cancellation.
